AVALON CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  TUESDAY, JUNE 16, 2026
  MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER – 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL – Present: Mayor Anni Marshall, Councilmembers De La Rosa, Lisa Lavelle,
Michael Ponce and Mary Schickling. Also present: City Manager David Maistros, City Attorney
Scott Campbell and Senior Management Analyst. Absent: City Clerk Gabrielle Morones.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS – City staff received 3 written communications regarding
Item #14. Adult-Use Cannabis Discussion. Copies were distributed to City Council and are on
file in the City Clerk’s office.

COUNCILMEMBER REQUESTS- Councilmember Lavelle requested that the following items
be placed on a future agenda for discussion:

  1. Potential penalties for residents who operate transportation services without the
  required transportation permit.
  2. Establish an appropriate waiting period, if any, before an individual who has operated
  illegally without a transportation permit may be eligible to apply for and obtain a
  transportation permit.

CONSENT CALENDAR-There were eight items on the Consent Calendar. Motion to approve
Items #1-#8 made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Mary Schickling. (All Ayes)

1.  Actions
  Approved minutes from the May 19, and June 2, 2026 regular City Council Meeting.

2.  Warrants
  Approved a US Bank General Account Warrants totaling $2,232,643.85, a US Bank LMI
  Housing Authority Warrants $146,477.31, three payrolls totaling $821,522.61, four
  electronic fund transfers totaling $425,707.52 for a total disbursement of $3,626,351.29
  for April 27, 2026 through May 29, 2026.

3.  Gann Appropriations Limit for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
  Adopted Resolution No. 26-18 of the City of Avalon Establishing an Appropriations Limit
  for Fiscal Year 2026/2027 Pursuant to Article XIII B of the California Constitution.

4.  Resolution Adopting List of Projects for Annual SB1 Allocation
  Adopted Resolution No. 26-19 of the City of Avalon Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal
  Year 2026-27 Funded by SB 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017.
  (June 16, 2026-5 Ayes-Marshall, De La Rosa, Lavelle, Ponce and Schickling)

5.  Adopt an Ordinance Prohibiting Fireworks in the City of Avalon
  Adopted Ordinance No. 1230-26 An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Avalon
  Prohibiting the Use, Possession, Sale, and Discharge of Fireworks within the City of
  Avalon.
 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 16, 2026
PAGE 2

6.  Award Professional Audit Services Contract
  Authorized the City Manager to execute a professional services agreement with DavisFarr
  LLP for professional auditing services for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, with the
  option of extending for the two (2) subsequent fiscal years.

7.  Cooperation Agreement for Continued Participation in the Los Angeles Urban County
  Community Development Block Grant Program
  Authorized the City Manager to execute the cooperation agreement with the Los Angeles
  County Development Authority for a three-year term beginning July 1, 2027 – June 30,
  2030.

8.  2026 Conflict of Interest Code-Biennial Notice
  Directed the City Clerk to notify all City Departments and advisory bodies that have
  previously adopted conflict of interest codes, of the biennial review requirements for such
  conflict of interest codes. Require all departments and advisory bodies that have
  previously adopted conflict of interest codes to review such conflict of interest codes and
  report to the City Council any amendments, or report that no amendments are necessary,
  no later than October 1, 2026.

PUBLIC HEARING

9.  Public Hearing and Submittal of Property Related Fees to Los Angeles County for FY26-
  27 Property Tax Roll – Sewer, Saltwater, and Solid Waste Fees
  1. Mayor Marshall opened a public hearing on whether to collect the annual trash
  collection service fees, grease collection service fees, sewer user fees, and saltwater
  charges, on the property tax roll by the County of Los Angeles.

  2. Comments were heard, and it was determined that there was not a majority protest
  filed. Mayor Marshall closed the public hearing and adopted the following four resolutions:

  Adopted Resolution No. 26-20 of the City Council of the City of Avalon Adopting the
  Report of the Annual Solid Waste Collection Service Fees and Directing the City Clerk
  of the City to File Said Report with the Los Angeles County Auditor and Request the
  Auditor Place the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Solid Waste Collection Service Fees on the
  Tax Roll.

  Adopted Resolution No. 26-21 of the City Council of the City of Avalon Adopting the
  Report of the Annual Grease Collection Service Fees and Directing the City Clerk of the
  City to File Said Report with the Los Angeles County Auditor and Request the Auditor
  Place the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Grease Collection Service Fees on the Tax Roll.
 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 16, 2026
PAGE 3

  Adopted Resolution No. 26-22 of the City Council of the City of Avalon Adopting the
  Report of the Annual Sewer User Fees and Directing the City Clerk of the City to File
  Said Report with the Los Angeles County Auditor and Request the Auditor Place the
  Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Sewer User Fees on the Tax Roll.

  Adopted Resolution No. 26-23 of the City Council of the City of Avalon Adopting the
  Report of The Annual Saltwater Charges and Directing the City Clerk of the City to File
  Said Report with the Los Angeles County Auditor and Request the Auditor Place the
  Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Saltwater Charges on the Tax Roll.

  3. City Council directed the City Clerk to request Los Angeles County to place the fees
  on the FY 2026/27 Property Tax Roll.

  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Michael Ponce.
  (4 Ayes-Marshall, De La Rosa, Lavelle and Ponce; 1 No-Schickling)

10.  Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Miscellaneous Fee Schedule
  1. City Council heard a presentation regarding the Miscellaneous Fee Schedule. 2.
  Mayor Marshall opened the Public Hearing; no comments were heard. 3. Mayor
  Marshall closed the Public Hearing. 4. Adopted Resolution No. 26-24 of the City Council
  of the City of Avalon Setting Fees for Services, Facilities and Activities of the City of
  Avalon for Fiscal Year 2026-27.

GENERAL BUSINESS

11.  Catalina Food Tours Transportation Permit Application
  1. City Council received presentation. 2. City Council discussed. 3. Approved the
  Transportation Permit for Catalina Food Tours to be added to the existing Residential
  Vehicle permit to conduct tours with stated conditions.
  City Council Member Lisa Lavelle recused herself due to a Conflict of Interest.
  Motion to approve made by Anni Marshall, seconded by Mary Schickling.
  (4 Ayes-Marshall, De La Rosa, Ponce and Schickling; 1 Abstention-Lavelle)

12.  Roger’s Guided Tours Transportation Permit Application
  1. City Council received presentation. 2. City Council discussed. 3. Approved the
  Transportation Permit for Roger’s Guided Tours utilizing one existing Residential Autoette
  permit to conduct tours with stated conditions.
  Motion to approve by Yesenia De La Rosa, seconded by Mary Schickling. (All Ayes)

13. Pebbly Beach Road Temporary Turn Around Installation and Traffic Safety Improvements
  Approved the plan as presented for modifications and striping along Pebbly Beach Road
  including installation of k-rail, signage and striping to install a temporary vehicle turn
  around.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Lisa Lavelle (All Ayes)
 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 16, 2026
PAGE 4

14.  Adult-Use Cannabis Discussion
  City Council reached consensus to not take any further action to pursue legalization of
  adult-use cannabis in Avalon.
  Motion to approve made by Anni Marshall, seconded by Michael Ponce.
  (3 Ayes-Marshall, De La Rosa, Ponce; 2 Noes-Lavelle and Schickling)

15.  Repair and Maintenance of City Shoreboat Float
  1. Amended the Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget, adding an additional $33,500 to account
  #10470-5705 to support the rehabilitation of the City-owned Shoreboat End Float. 2.
  Ratified prior action and authorized an additional expenditure of an amount not-to-exceed
  $33,346.36 to Al Larson Boat Shop, a sole source vender, for the rehabilitation of the
  City-owned Shore-boat Float for a total repair of $93,346.36.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa. (All Ayes)

16.  Award to DCCM for Project Management Services
  1. Made the affirmative finding the City will not gain a competitive advantage through a
  separate competitive solicitation and that the required services can be obtained more
  economically and efficiently pursuant to Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111(C); 2.
  Awarded a Professional Services Agreement to DCCM to provide Project Management
  Services for the Pebbly Beach Landfill Life Site Optimization Project and related on-call
  consulting services in an amount not-to-exceed $200,000 annually; and 3. Authorized the
  City Manager to execute the Agreement and any related documents, including
  amendments within the approved contract authority.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa. (All Ayes)

17.  Contract for Stage 1 Design and Engineering Services Progressive Design-Build Contract
  for the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization Project Phase 2
  Authorized the City Manager to finalize negotiations and execute the Stage 1 design and
  engineering services progressive design-build contract for the Cabrillo Mole Revitalization
  Phase 2 Project with Anderson Burton Construction, Inc. for a not-to-exceed sum of $1.8
  million.
  Motion to approve made by Lisa Lavelle, seconded by Michael Ponce. (All Ayes)

  BREAK 7:49 p.m.-7:56 p.m.

18.  Proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget
  City Council continued discussing the proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget.
  City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-25 of the City Council of the City of Avalon
  Adopting the Budget for Fiscal Year 2026-27.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Yesenia De La Rosa. (All Ayes)
 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 16, 2026
PAGE 5

CLOSED SESSION-8:30 p.m.-8:50 p.m.

Following the appropriate announcement of the Closed Session items the City Council went into
Closed Session to discuss the following:

  1. Conference with legal counsel—anticipated litigation
  Gov’t Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): 2 cases
  The City has received two letters from Lance Ware, one dated May 29, 2026
  and the other dated June 3, 2026 threatening litigation. Copies of the letters
  (without any exhibits) are attached and are also available for public
  inspection with exhibits pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.5.

Following Closed Session, the City Attorney announced that the City Council unanimously
authorized the City Attorney to file papers with the federal communications commission.

Mayor Marshall adjourned the meeting at 9:09 p.m.

I, Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk, do hereby certify that the digital recording of the regular City
Council Meeting on June 16, 2026, is the official record of the Council Meeting and is on file and
maintained in City Hall.

_________________________________
Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk
   AVALON SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  THURSDAY, JUNE 25, 2026
  MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER – 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL – Present: Mayor Anni Marshall, Councilmembers Lisa Lavelle, Michael Ponce
and Mary Schickling. Also present: City Manager David Maistros, City Attorney Scott
Campbell and Senior Management Analyst. Absent: Councilmembers De La Rosa.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS – City Staff received one (1) written communication regarding
Item #1 Direction on City Action in Response to May 29, 2026 Demand for Cure and Correct
Letter and Unconditional Commitment Letter and 22 written communications regarding Item #2
Rescission of the May 22, 2026 Letter to the Federal Communications Commission and
Direction Filing Responses to the Federal Communications Commission in Response to Filing
of AVX.

GENERAL BUSINESS

1.  Direction on City Action in Response to May 29, 2026 Demand for Cure and Correct Letter
  and Unconditional Commitment Letter
  Authorized the City Attorney to Prepare an Unconditional Commitment Letter in response
  to the May 29, 2026 Demand for Cure and Correct Letter.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Lisa Lavelle.
  (4 Ayes – Marshall, Lavelle, Ponce and Schickling, 1 Absent – De La Rosa)

2.  Rescission of the May 22, 2026 Letter to the Federal Communications Commission and
  Direction Filing Responses to the Federal Communications Commission in Response to
  Filing of AVX
  Rescinded the May 22, 2026 letter to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
  and authorized the City Attorney to file responses to AVX’s filings with the FCC.
  Motion to approve made by Michael Ponce, seconded by Lisa Lavelle.
  (4 Ayes – Marshall, Lavelle, Ponce and Schickling, 1 Absent – De La Rosa)

Mayor Marshall adjourned the meeting at 5:17 p.m.

I, Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk, do hereby certify that the digital recording of the regular City
Council Meeting on June 16, 2026, is the official record of the Council Meeting and is on file and
maintained in City Hall.

_________________________________
Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk
